headline: The proposal's real idea on my lens is that **the routing key is a point in outcome space, and the device sequence is a derivation the user never has to name**. Ours is the inverse: `itemPaths` enumerates device combinations (`comboMethodEntry` label = literally "סו-ויד + עישון"), and CP2's approved row shows icons + `68°/30ש → 120°/1.5ש` + a citation marker — five schedules and not one word about what any of them tastes or feels like. We are not merely missing the UI: `svOrderDesc()` (app.js:3839) returns the exact outcome copy this feature needs ("maximal smoke ring", "flavor and crust") and has **zero callers anywhere in app.js or tests** — we wrote it and never rendered it. But the two models are not actually in tension, because the outcome vector belongs to the **citation**, not to the engine: we already do this correctly on exactly one axis — `doneness` lets the user pick a texture goal and moves the target temp by reading a **cited per-level table** (`doneness.levels.mr.c=54`), never a formula. Generalize that pattern to five more axes and outcome-driven routing becomes cited-only ranking over the existing `itemPaths` set, with zero new schedule math. The honest cost is authoring: their model computes outcomes in O(1), ours must cite them per (item, path).

conceptsFound.concept: Outcome space as the routing key — the user states a result, the engine derives the path (§2.3, §3.2)
conceptsFound.steelman: The decision a cook actually faces is 'bark or juice? tonight or tomorrow? fall-apart or sliceable?' — not 'sous-vide+smoke or smoke-only'. Make the outcome the addressable object: a small closed vector (texture, crust, smoke intensity, chew risk, juiciness, attention) is the primary key; the device sequence is a derivation, an implementation detail the interface can hide entirely. Device vocabulary then appears only where it must (what to plug in), never where a choice is made. The same vocabulary is reusable across all 130 cuts, which is what makes the per-card prose shrinkable.
conceptsFound.value: A user standing at a smoker at 06:00 picks by the thing they care about. Today the CP2 panel asks them to infer outcome from two temperatures and a duration. Adapted (not adopted) because our doctrine forbids DERIVING a path from an outcome — only RANKING cited paths by outcome fit.

Our bulk is the 279 CITATIONS, which are irreducible by construction. Where the insight DOES apply is the free prose: 85 lines of data.py carry outcome vocabulary ('בקליפה לעסיסיות', 'יותר=גומי', 'פריך מבחוץ') as untranslatable per-item strings that a closed outcome vocabulary would replace with tags — that is the shrink worth taking, and it's a side-effect of the outcome layer, not a separate project.

conceptsFound.steelman: Seasoning is a plugin that changes taste without changing thermodynamics; keep the two in separate namespaces so a flavor choice can never move a temperature and a physics change can never silently alter a flavor claim.

The one genuine graft from their §7 is the interaction rules (no oil in the sous-vide bag; cut seasoning 30% under vacuum; no sugar above 120°C before the smoke ring sets) — those are physics×flavor couplings we do not encode.

whereItBeatsUs:
Four places, stated without hedging.

**1. Our path labels are device names, at the exact moment a choice is made.** `comboMethodEntry` (app.js:3780) builds the label as `combo.map(m=>names[m]).join(' + ')` — "סו-ויד + עישון". `itemPaths` (app.js:4175) passes it through. The approved CP2 row (`mockups/cp2/variant-b-list.html`, rowHTML) renders icons + that label + `pathFigures` + `pathCiteHTML`. A brisket card will show five rows of two temperatures each and **no statement of what any of them produces**. Their §8 step 3 shows three outcomes and hides every number until the dashboard. For a real user at a smoker, theirs is better.

**2. We authored the outcome copy and never shipped it.** `SV_SMOKE_ORDERS` (app.js:3823) carries `desc`/`descEn` per order — "מתבשל לדיוק ומפוסטר בסו-ויד, ואז מקבל טעם וקראסט", "עישון על בשר גולמי לטבעת-עשן מרבית". `svOrderDesc(k)` (app.js:3839) reads them. `grep -n "svOrderDesc" app.js tests/*.ts` returns **one line: the definition.** Zero callers. This is not a design disagreement; it is a shipped omission on precisely the axis this panel is about.

**3. We have no texture/crust/chewiness axis, and the one we have is crippled.** `doneness` covers steak-like cuts only, moves a temperature only, and is **session-scoped** — `currentDoneness` reads `cardGet(doneKey(cut))` with the comment "session-only: template resets on next visit" (app.js:3031). There is no pulled-vs-sliceable, no bark-vs-bare, no chew risk, nowhere. `filters.time` and `filters.diff` (app.js:2394-2398) are real time and effort budgets — and they filter WHICH CUTS APPEAR IN THE CATALOG, never which path inside a cut. We already compute per-method lead time in `leadForMethod` and throw it away one level above where it matters.

**4. A cited outcome verdict currently loses to a category heuristic — and I can name the three items.** `sources.py` carries `grillable: False` on 25 cuts with explicit reasons. `methodRules(c)` (app.js:989) branches on `isProduce` / `isOffal` / `c.doneness` and **never reads `c.grillable`**; only `grillLine` (app.js:2822) reads it, and only to print a sentence. For 22 of the 25 the collagen branch happens to agree. For **three it does not**: Goose Liver (#74, "NOT grilled — rendering fat flares on open grate"), Veal Brain (#80, "NOT grillable — too soft/custardy for grates") and Whole Smoked Garlic (#102, "not direct-grilled") all fall to `isOffal`/`isProduce`, whose rule is `{allowed:['sv','smoke','grill'], def:['grill'], invalid:[]}` — so **grill-only is enumerated AND is their default path**, against a cited source that says don't. That is exactly the failure their Rule 1 is designed to prevent, and their worse-engineered version is structurally right where ours is wrong: the outcome verdict must be the router.
whereWeAreBetter:
**Path existence is cited; theirs is generated.** `itemPaths` derives strictly from `itemProfile` + the `order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv` citation blocks. If no source backs a schedule, the path does not exist. Their `generateRecipePipeline` emits `chamber_temp: "110°C"` from a code branch; §4.4 converts a 10-hour cook to 1h12m via a bare `0.12` multiplier. Under our doctrine that number cannot ship. This is not defensiveness — it is why outcome-driven *generation* is unadoptable here and outcome-driven *ranking* is.

**Equipment↔path correlation, the owner's point 4, is already ours by a wide margin.** `eqmValidity` (app.js:1858) evaluates ownership across every enumerated path — not the default only — producing `okPaths`, per-kind `gaps` with `missing` vs `partial` distinguished, an orthogonal probe gap (O-7), and a `fixes` ladder ordered by cheapness, all cached by kit generation. Theirs is one `INTERSECT` and a `throw`. Beyond it we model what they don't model at all: occupancy by **area** (`footprint_cm2 = kg × cm²/kg` by shape class) rather than weight, hanging-vs-shelf as an optimization move, sous-vide bath sharing gated on setpoint equality (`cookerContention`), and availability as free/partial/busy over a time window with the negative case (D11) explicitly tested. Their §5 allocates shelf area and calls it done.

**Order-specific cited schedules with their own safety flags.** `order_smokesv` carries `{smoke:{t:75,h:'1.5-2',cold:false}, sv:{t:68,h:'30',pasteurize:true}}` with a Baldwin ref; `itemStages` reads the cited values and falls back to a conservative computed value only when data is absent, and labels honor the citation's own `cold` flag rather than assuming. Their equivalent for the same trade-off is a multiplier.

**The flavor axis.** 354 tagged seasonings (flavor / base / heat / cats) behind a live five-axis filter versus their three-row table — and our flavor/physics separation is actually clean, where their PREFERENCE_FLAVOR token ("Smoky_And_Crusty") smuggles a texture into the flavor namespace.

**One axis of their own model, already built correctly.** `doneness` IS outcome-driven routing done right: the user picks a texture word, and `donenessTarget` reads a **cited per-level table** to move the target. The user never sees a formula and the app never invents a temperature. That is the template for everything below.
proposedModel:
**Thesis: outcome-driven routing and cited-only paths are compatible, because the outcome vector belongs to the CITATION, not to the engine. The engine never derives a schedule from an outcome; it derives a RANKING. The path set stays exactly `itemPaths`. No new schedule math, no new number.**

## 1. Data — one new cited block, through the existing pipeline

Extend the research-JSON → `gen_sources.py` route (same road `order_smokesv` travelled), so a new outcome vector is **data + citation, zero JS** — CP3's acceptance bar already demands that.

```python
# sources.py, per cut, keyed by the SAME path id itemPaths emits
'path_outcomes': {
  'c:smoke_sv': {                      # forward sv→smoke
    'texture':   'sliceable',          # pulled | sliceable | tender-juicy | firm-bite | crisp-skin
    'crust':     'bark-firm',          # none | light-color | bark-soft | bark-firm | crackling
    'smoke':     2,                    # 0..3 delivered by THIS path
    'juice':     3,                    # 0..3
    'chew_risk': 0,                    # 0..3  — the owner's לעיסתיות
    'attention': 1,                    # 0..3  hands-on interventions
    'ref': '...', 'url': '...', 'note': 'why these values'
  },
  'c:smoke_sv:rev': {...}, 'c:smoke': {...}
}
```

Two axes are **derived, never authored**, so they cannot drift:
- `time_h` = `Σ stage.hours` from `effectiveSchedule(meta, sel)` — already exact.
- `devices` = `deriveRequires(meta, methodKey, order)` — already exact.

**The citation rule that keeps this inside DoD-10 (and caps the authoring cost):** *any attribute that BLOCKS or DEMOTES a path must be cited; any attribute that merely DESCRIBES a path may be derived, and must render visually distinct (muted, no ✓ mark).* So `chew_risk` and `grillable` are cited; `texture`/`crust`/`smoke`/`attention` may be derived from the path's own shape (a path whose sv leg is ≥68°/≥20h on a collagen cut is `pulled`; a path ending in ≥110° smoke for ≥1h has `bark-firm`) with a per-item cited override. That collapses authoring from ~650 blocks to ~130 chew verdicts — of which **25 already exist** as `grillable:False` plus free-text `src.grill.note`. This mirrors our existing AI doctrine exactly: the AI ranks among solver-emitted moves and is never the source of a number.

## 2. The user's parameter set — 5 questions, all optional, all defaulted

| # | Question (he) | Values | Default | Router use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | איך שיהיה המרקם? | מפורק · פרוס · רך-עסיסי · נגיסה מוצקה | *the item's current default path's own texture* | rank; hard filter only if set explicitly |
| 2 | קרום? | בלי · קל · קרום מלא · פריך | קרום מלא when a smoke path exists, else קל | rank |
| 3 | כמה זמן יש לך? | ≤2ש · ≤6ש · ≤12ש · ≤24ש · לא משנה | **inherit `serve − now` when an event is open**, else לא משנה | hard filter on Σ stage.hours |
| 4 | כמה תשומת-לב? | שגר ושכח · בינוני · אני ליד | בינוני | rank on `attention` |
| 5 | עוצמת עשן? | 0..3 · לא משנה | לא משנה | rank on `smoke` |

Plus a sixth never asked and always applied: **the kit you own** (`eqmValidity.okPaths`).

**The invariance clause that makes this shippable without a big bang — and it is testable:** with every answer at its default, `rankPaths` MUST return today's `itemPaths` order with today's default first, byte-identical. This is the same invariance CP2 Task 1 already established for the stored default; the outcome layer inherits it or it does not ship.

Storage: the Phase-3a `PREFS` registry (already owner-approved), so defaults reproduce current behavior exactly and everything is opt-in.

## 3. The functions — pure, no schedule math

```js
outcomePrefs()                 // → {texture, crust, timeH, attention, smoke}  from PREFS
pathOutcome(meta, p)           // → the cited-or-derived outcome block for path p, or null
rankPaths(meta, prefs, kit)    // → [{ p, fit, why[], cost[], blocked }]
```

`rankPaths` returns per path:
- `fit` — used ONLY for ordering. **Never rendered as a number** (a score invites the user to read it as precision we don't have).
- `why[]` — the axes this path wins on, as short phrases: `['פרוס', 'קרום מלא', 'עשן ●●○']`.
- `cost[]` — the axes it loses vs the top-ranked path. **This is the LOSS_OF_ATTR vector, derived rather than authored:** `['מהיר ב-9ש', 'בלי קרום', 'סיכון לעיסתיות ↑']`.
- `blocked` — `null` | `{reason:'kit'|'time'|'chew', text, cite}`. **Blocked paths stay in the list, greyed, with the reason** — their §11 scenario B behavior, which is better than our current silent deletion.

Division of labor, unchanged and enforced: **`methodRules`/`validCombo` decide EXISTENCE; `rankPaths` decides ORDER and EXPLANATION.** One correction to existence: `methodRules` must read `c.grillable` and let the cited verdict outrank the category heuristic — that alone fixes Goose Liver / Veal Brain / Whole Smoked Garlic defaulting to a grill their own sources forbid.

## 4. CP2 — concrete recommendation: reshape the row, do not replace the panel

Tasks 1, 2, 4–9 are correct substrate; keep them exactly as approved. Then:

1. **Task 3 row gains one line** — `.cp-why`, between `.crtitle` and `.crfig`: 2–4 outcome chips from `pathOutcome`. Where no outcome block exists yet the line renders **empty, never invented**. CP3's research batch then lights it up per item with zero JS.
2. **The closed head shows a delta, not just the default.** Today: "🌊💨 סו-ויד → עישון · ברירת מחדל". Proposed, when prefs are set: "· 2 מסלולים מתאימים יותר למה שביקשת". That is the discovery hook the panel currently has none of ("5 מסלולים" is a count, not a reason to tap).
3. **New `#cpWant` strip above the panel** — the five questions as chips, collapsed to one line ("מה בא לך? ▾"), all defaulted. Setting a chip **re-ranks and re-labels; it never auto-selects a path.** This is the deliberate safety divergence from the proposal, which auto-selects.
4. **`eqmValidity.fixes` switch-path labels become outcome-labelled.** Today: `'זמין במסלול: ' + p.label`. Proposed: `'זמין במסלול: סו-ויד → עישון · פרוס, קרום מלא · +9ש'`. Same function, same ordering, richer label from the same `pathOutcome`.
5. **Wire `svOrderDesc` into the row, or delete it.** It is dead code holding exactly this copy.

**Sequencing, and the Waiver Gate (§4) said out loud:** CP2's approved plan contains no outcome content whatsoever. Items 1, 2, 4, 5 are small and could ride CP2; item 3 is genuinely new UX and needs a mockup + owner visual approval per §10.9. **Either way this is a change to an approved spec and must be raised with the owner in conversation — recording it here does not count.** My recommendation: ship CP2 exactly as approved, then **CP2b** = items 1/2/4/5 + the `grillable` fix, then **CP3** carries the research batch AND the `#cpWant` strip.

## 5. Does ranking lose the point? Honestly: it loses coverage, not the point.

Their engine can answer "fast pulled brisket" for which no source exists — by synthesizing one. Ours answers "no cited path reaches that; the closest is X, and it costs you 8 hours." **For a safety-bearing app that is the correct behavior and the more honest one.** The remedy for coverage is the CP3 research track, already planned. The framing worth giving the owner: outcome-driven routing turns the research backlog from an internal list into a **user-visible coverage metric** — "we cover 3 of 5 texture goals for brisket" — which is the first time that work has had a legible unit.
openQuestions: Does the outcome vector attach to the (item, path) PAIR or to the path SHAPE alone? Per-pair is accurate but ~650 blocks; per-shape with per-item overrides is ~20x cheaper. My proposal assumes shape-derived + cited override, but the owner should rule on whether a DERIVED descriptive tag may render at all next to cited figures, even when visually distinguished.

Where do the five questions live — per item (the card, as the proposal does), per event, or per user profile? Our PREFS registry is per-user; `mk-tlstate-<evScope>` is per-occurrence. An event-level 'tonight I want fast' seems most useful and reuses existing storage, but it splits the answer from the card where the choice is made.

Should question 3 (time budget) DEFAULT to the open event's `serve − now`? We already compute backward schedules, so this is a free and real budget — but it means the panel silently re-ranks when the clock moves, which may read as instability.

When an outcome preference blocks a path (chew risk), is it hard-blocked or selectable-with-confirmation? Today `validCombo` hard-removes it and says nothing. Greyed-with-reason is strictly better; selectable-with-confirmation is a separate call.

Does `doneness` become axis #1 (texture) for steak-like cuts, or stay a separate control? Merging is cleaner UX, but `doneness` legitimately MOVES a cited temperature while the other five axes only rank — collapsing them risks blurring the exact line this whole design rests on.

Is `chew_risk` a safety-adjacent claim or a quality claim? I proposed 'any attribute that blocks or demotes must be cited' as the line. If the owner rules it purely quality, the authoring cost drops further but a derived value could talk a user out of a path with no source behind it.

The `grillable` fix changes the DEFAULT path of three shipped items (#74 Goose Liver, #80 Veal Brain, #102 Whole Smoked Garlic) from grill-only to something else. That is a behavior change on cited grounds, and it needs its own regression red-green plus a check of what `deriveRequires`/`eqmValidity` then say for those three.
